actual_tested_facet_map.target: PIL relaxes traditional locus standi for genuine public injury. A public-spirited person may approach the court for disadvantaged persons unable to seek relief themselves.
The petitioner must act bona fide and demonstrate genuine public interest. Courts may reject frivolous, publicity-oriented or politically motivated PILs and impose costs.
PIL is also called social action litigation.
Articles 32 and 226 are the principal constitutional routes for PIL in the Supreme Court and High Courts.
Epistolary jurisdiction allows an appropriate communication to be treated as a petition in a genuine case.
PIL is primarily remedial and may be less strictly adversarial than ordinary private litigation.
A public-spirited person may approach the court for disadvantaged persons unable to seek relief themselves.
PIL is not meant to settle purely private disputes or personal grievances.
Courts may reject frivolous, publicity-oriented or politically motivated PILs and impose costs.
A policy disagreement alone is insufficient; a judicially reviewable illegality or constitutional violation is required.
The supplied account credits Krishna Iyer and Bhagwati as pioneers of Indian PIL.
Social Interest Litigation(SIL) is another label used for PIL in the supplied account. Class Action Litigation(CAL) is another label used for PIL in the supplied account.
Cooperative parties andretention ofjudicial procedure; notmerely genericremedial orientation.
SC letter-PIL guidelines recognise minimum-wage, casual-worker exploitation and labour-law complaints, except individual cases.

Neglected children are a recognised letter-PIL category. Specified harassment/torture of villagers, particularly SC/ST and economically backward groups, is recognised. Petitions from riot victims are a recognised letter-PIL category.

Specified police refusal to register cases, harassment and custodial-death complaints are recognised. Atrocities against women are a recognised letter-PIL category. The guidelines recognise public-importance pollution, ecology, drugs, food-adulteration, heritage, culture, antiques, forest and wildlife matters.

The guideline footnote permits direct SC consideration of serious torture, custody-death and similar allegations. The footnote ordinarily routes premature-release/parole matters to the concerned HC rather than treating every such matter as an Article 32 petition.
Family pension is expressly included among ordinarily entertained letter-PIL categories. Ordinary service, pension and gratuity matters are excluded, read with the specific family-pension entry.

Government-department/local-body complaints are excluded except those within the recognised categories. Medical and other educational admission matters are excluded from these letter-PIL categories. Requests for early hearing in pending HC/subordinate-court cases are excluded from these letter-PIL categories.
Case/framework associations;years supplied in stem,not independently assessed.
Application of res judicata or analogous preclusion to PIL depends on the petition's nature and case facts; neither automatic absence nor universal application follows.
A purely private dispute is not PIL; an appropriate case arising from a personal grievance may nevertheless justify examining broader public affairs in the interest of justice.
In special PIL situations, a Commission or other body may investigate allegations and find facts; allegations are not thereby presumed proved.

Chaufal calls for proper High Court PIL rules rather than each judge devising a personal procedure. Chaufal prioritises larger public interest, gravity and urgency rather than publicity or private gain.
Distinguish monetary/private leverage and privileged-convenience criticisms from a categorical filing ban by wealth or class.
